explanations.answer: Their faith in the Lord Jesus and their love for all the saints
explanations.explanation: That's the news that reached Paul, friend: "…your faith in the Lord Jesus and your love for all the saints…" (Ephesians 1:15). Faith in Jesus and love for God's people, both in one sentence. I think that's the kind of report that makes a person grab a pencil and start a prayer list.

explanations.answer: Their courage in prison and their gifts to the poor in Jerusalem
explanations.explanation: Good guess, but that's not in this passage. What Paul heard about is their faith in the Lord Jesus and their love for all the saints (Ephesians 1:15). Courage in prison and gifts for the poor aren't mentioned in these verses. These folks in Ephesus get their own headline right here.

explanations.answer: Their bold preaching in the city and their care for widows
explanations.explanation: Nope, friend, that's not on Paul's list. He says he heard about "…your faith in the Lord Jesus and your love for all the saints…" (Ephesians 1:15). Preaching and widows are good things, but the text doesn't name them here. I once stamped a whole batch before reading the recipe, so I get it.

Yes, friend, yes! Paul prays for "…a spirit of wisdom and revelation in your knowledge of Him." (Ephesians 1:17). The wisdom is about knowing God Himself. He's asking the glorious Father to give it, and that's the whole point.

explanations.answer: In their plans for the year ahead
explanations.explanation: I love a good plan, but that's not what Paul is asking for. He prays for "…a spirit of wisdom and revelation in your knowledge of Him." (Ephesians 1:17). The "Him" is God. Calendars and planners can stay in the drawer on this one, and I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, so I know a thing or two about drawers.

explanations.answer: In their dealings with city leaders
explanations.explanation: Not quite, friend. The text says wisdom and revelation "…in your knowledge of Him." (Ephesians 1:17). It doesn't mention city leaders at all. Paul's prayer is aimed at knowing God, and he asks the Father to do the giving.

Careful, friend, this one slips past you fast. Paul doesn't ask for their eyesight to be healed. He asks that "…the eyes of your heart may be enlightened…" (Ephesians 1:18). It's the heart's eyes, so this isn't about a trip to the eye doctor.

That's right, it's False. Paul prays for "…the eyes of your heart…" to be enlightened (Ephesians 1:18), not for their eyes to be healed. Nothing in the text talks about eyesight here. He wants them to know something, and he says what in the next verses.

explanations.answer: The hope of His calling and the greatness of His power
explanations.explanation: There it is! Paul names "the hope of His calling, the riches of His glorious inheritance in the saints, and the surpassing greatness of His power to us who believe" (Ephesians 1:18-19). You picked two of the three, and the three are all in there. That's a lot of knowing packed into one prayer.

explanations.answer: The secret of being content in every season
explanations.explanation: That one sounds nice, but it's not on Paul's list here. In this prayer he names "…the hope of His calling…" "…the riches of His glorious inheritance in the saints…" and "…the surpassing greatness of His power to us who believe." (Ephesians 1:18-19). Contentment is a good topic, just not this one.

explanations.answer: The plans of every enemy coming against them
explanations.explanation: Whoa, friend, Paul never goes there in this prayer. He asks that they would know "…the hope of His calling…" and "…the surpassing greatness of His power to us who believe." (Ephesians 1:18-19). The text doesn't mention enemies or their plans. He keeps his eyes on God's calling, God's inheritance and God's power.

explanations.answer: He raised Him from the dead and seated Him at His right hand
explanations.explanation: That's it! God's mighty strength was exerted in Christ "…when He raised Him from the dead and seated Him at His right hand in the heavenly realms…" (Ephesians 1:20). Raised and seated, both in one verse. That's strength I can't even bake a joke about.

explanations.answer: He kept Him safe from every enemy He faced on the earth
explanations.explanation: Close to the neighborhood, but not the address. Paul says God raised Christ "…from the dead…" and seated Him "…at His right hand in the heavenly realms…" (Ephesians 1:20). The text doesn't say anything about keeping Him safe from enemies here. Raising Him from the dead is a whole different level.

explanations.answer: He carried Him up to heaven in a chariot of fire
explanations.explanation: Ooh, friend, you've got your fire chariot mixed up! Paul says God "…raised Him from the dead and seated Him at His right hand in the heavenly realms…" (Ephesians 1:20). There's no chariot in this verse. A chariot of fire does show up for Elijah, the prophet, in 2 Kings 2:11, but that's his story.

True, friend! Christ is seated "…far above all rule and authority, power and dominion, and every name that is named, not only in the present age but also in the one to come." (Ephesians 1:21). Right now and the age to come, both covered. Paul says it reaches into both.

Not this time, friend. Paul says Christ is far above every name that is named, "…not only in the present age but also in the one to come." (Ephesians 1:21). So it does reach into the age to come. It's True, and I'd say it with my whole mustache.

Right on the dough! Christ is head over everything for the church, "…which is His body…" (Ephesians 1:22-23). Head and body, right there together in one breath. I think that's a picture worth chewing on slowly.

I get why you went there, friend. But "bride" isn't the word Paul uses in this passage. Here he says the church "…is His body…" (Ephesians 1:23). Christ is made head over everything for the church, and the word right next to it is body.

That's another picture people use for God's people, but it's not the one in these verses. Paul says the church "…is His body…" (Ephesians 1:23). Christ is made head over everything for the church, and the word right next to it is body.
